title: ERYMON: The Long Way Home – A creature-collecting RPG. Not the kind you remember.
author: Revolutionary_Fun574

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/Revolutionary_Fun574 please share some more about how you used AI in developing this. Naming the tools or saying "made with AI" doesn't count. Rule 4 is how we keep promotional posts contributing, by having them talk about the process and how the game was made. Trying to keep the sub focused on dev. This post may be removed if it isn't updated.

replies.author: Revolutionary_Fun574
replies.body:
Thanks for the heads-up! Here's how AI fit into the process:

\*\*Art:\*\* \[e.g. I generated base sprites / tilesets with X, then cleaned them up by hand: fixed palettes, redrew outlines, resized to the grid, made walk cycles consistent\]. The hardest part was \[e.g. keeping characters consistent across frames\], which I solved by \[...\].

\*\*Code:\*\* \[e.g. the game is built in X. I used AI to help write Y (battle system / dialogue system / save system), then debugged and restructured it myself\]. Biggest issue: \[...\].

\*\*Writing / story:\*\* \[e.g. the story, world and lore ("Erymon are life that learned to drink the Aether") are mine; I used AI to help with Z or not at all\].

\*\*What I did by hand:\*\* \[design, level layout, balancing, music, etc.\]

\*\*What I learned:\*\* \[one honest lesson, e.g. "AI gets you a first draft fast, but most of the time went into making everything feel like the same game."\]

Happy to go deeper on any part!
